text.p: Following are some of the main stories in Dutch newspapers today. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
HET FINANCIEELE DAGBLAD
- Post and telecom group KPN makes friendly offer of Dfl 2.7 bn in cash to buy Australian transport group TNT. (p1)
- Financial services group Fortis talks with ABN Amro bank on takeover of its merchant banking unit MeesPierson. (p1)
- Philips Electronics and KPN at loggerheads over merger of their cable activities. (p1)
- Coalition parties agree to differ on MPs combining parliamentary work with a position on a company's supervisory board. (p1)
- Aalberts Industries to make a major takeover of Germany's Seppelfricke Armaturengruppe. (p3)
- Unilever is to merge Van den Bergh and Unilever Vlees Groep (UVG) costing 70 jobs. (p4)
- ABN Amro bank is upbeat about earnings of entertainment group Endemol, soon to be launched on ASE. (p5)
- Telecom arm of KPN looks at possibility of participating in imminent partial privatisation of South Africa's Telkom. (p5) DE VOLKSKRANT
- Dutch gravestone industry worried about cheap imported stones from India. (p2)
- Finance minister Gerrit Zalm lashes out at the U.S. for claiming the leading role in international funds they do not contribute to. (p2)
- Aalberts Industries to issue new shares to finance takeover of Seppelfricke. (p21) DE TELEGRAAF
- Job growth in Amsterdam area to continue up to the year 2010 mainly through positive office buildings market. (p9)
- Parliament urges economic affairs minister Hans Wijers to to get talks going again with Samsung on Fokker takeover. (p21)
- Belgian temp agency Creyf's to expand in the Netherlands by taking over Van den Boom of Brabant. (p35)
- Transavia Airlines, 80 pct KLM-owned, to be screened by accountancy group Coopers & Lybrand. (p35) TROUW
- More than half of Unilever's Dutch food production is loss-giving according to Unilever chief. (p6) ALGEMEEN DAGBLAD
- Philips Electronics' main problem of expansion in Asia is getting enough qualified staff. (p10)
- City of Rotterdam to start experiment with unmanned container vehicles in its harbour. (p12)
